text:
Priya Patel: Starting EU-WEST9 H100p cluster bring-up now, hitting a couple of blockers during bootstrap. posting root logs and short summary.

Alex Chen: ok — what are the symptoms?

Priya Patel: nodes provisioned but many show NotReady and kubelet logs show CNI errors + OOM for kube-proxy in some replicas. Also AWS API returned a couple of ENI quota errors during attach.

Danielle: ENI quota? we usually hit that when using dedicated subnets for GPU-sized instances. Can you paste the cloud errors?

Priya Patel: here's the AWS error we saw during node join: 

```
An error occurred (InstanceLimitExceeded) when calling the CreateNetworkInterface operation: The maximum number of network interfaces has been reached for the instance type
```

Priya Patel: and kubectl: 

```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide
NAME                          STATUS     ROLES    AGE    VERSION   INTERNAL-IP    EXTERNAL-IP
h100p-node-1                  NotReady   <none>   12m    v1.27.3   10.10.5.12     3.5.6.7
h100p-node-2                  Ready      <none>   10m    v1.27.3   10.10.5.13     3.5.6.8
```

Alex Chen: sounds like subnet-level ENI/IPv4 address exhaustion for older instance-family mappings. Did the terraform module create the expected /27 per AZ?

Priya Patel: terraform created /26 per AZ (we used the standard template), but the H100p flavor requires multiple ENIs for GPUDirect/placement group networking and our secondary IP spare pool is small.

Sasha: another angle — I saw MTU mismatches on the VPC side when we switched the CNI to the new eniflex plugin. That causes packet fragmentation and the kube-proxy healthchecks fail. Priya, can you share dmesg/kmod logs for nvidia?

Priya Patel: pasted nvidia kernel errors: 

```
[ 1234.567890] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
[ 1234.568123] nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel.
[ 1235.001200] peer memory initialization failed: -22
```

Danielle: peer memory failing is usually because iptables/nft or CNI blocked vfio/ib verbs init. Could be the ENI attach order race.

infra-bot: Deploy check: aws-eni-allocator failed 2/3 times; automatic retry scheduled in 30s.

Morgan: we should avoid churn — recommendation: 1) revert to old aws-cni on this ASG, 2) request temporary ENI quota bump for the region, 3) switch initial batch to on-demand instances (not spot) until bootstrap green.

Alex Chen: I agree on reverting CNI first to stop the fragmentation. Priya, can you run a quick test by tainting new nodes and spinning up 1 control-plane-subnet-only node with older CNI?

Priya Patel: doing that now. also tagging cloud ticket to request ENI limit increase. ticket# CW-5921.

Priya Patel: quick test results: single node with aws-cni reverted comes up Ready, nv_peer_memory init ok, no ENI errors on attach. So CNI is a major contributor.

Sasha: good. For the quota increase, what's the ask? how many extra ENIs/secondary IPs?

Priya Patel: asking +50 ENIs / AZ and +200 secondary addresses across the region to be safe while we validate.

oncall: note — handoff checklist for first live cluster: 1) quotas confirmed, 2) CNI pinned and validated, 3) kernel modules validated on AMI, 4) reserved capacity pricing confirmed, 5) smoke tests passing. I added the checklist to the runbook.

Alex Chen: pricing — do we proceed with reserved or on-demand for initial 20 nodes? using reserved requires procurement lead time.

Morgan: finance prefers to start on-demand for 2 weeks while we complete validation; cost delta acceptable vs risk of rollback & repeated provisioning attempts. we'll convert to reserved once SLOs stable.

Priya Patel: plan going forward: 1) revert CNI on ASG (done), 2) run 4-node health validation (running), 3) wait for ENI quota bump, 4) once green, remove taint and scale to 20 nodes on on-demand for 48h, 5) handoff to platform with runbook link and ticket ids.

Danielle: make sure AMI has nvidia-driver v550 and nv_peer_memory module enabled in init scripts — we had a previous drift where packaging missed that.

Priya Patel: noted — updating AMI bake and adding an automated smoke that checks `nvidia-smi` + `dmesg` for peer mem lines.

Alex Chen: any chance application teams need to be paused for the rollout?

Priya Patel: not yet — we'll do staging only. if we hit instability we'll notify product and pause.

Sasha: adding a postmortem template section to runbook for CNI experiments so we capture lessons (kernel versions, MTU, ENI counts).

Priya Patel: final: rolling back to old CNI made bootstrap succeed — continuing with validation. I'll post an update once we finish the 4-node smoke. :thumbsup:
